links.outcome: 6-month semaglutide adherence before vs after AI support agent, adjusted and matched
links.effect: Unadjusted adherence 53.2% vs 47.3% (p<0.001), but adjusted post-Junebot era had higher odds of attrition (OR 1.178; 95% CI 1.052-1.318); era-matched PSM OR 1.309 (p=0.038).
links.quote: Integrating an AI digital assistant did not independently improve medication adherence; programmatic costs, program pauses and initial tracking anxiety were stronger predictors of long-term retention.

screen.reason: Retrospective evaluation of a real-world deployment of an AI conversational agent (Junebot) for patient support in a digital obesity clinic, comparing retention pre- and post-integration.
